items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone vs Standard Treatment for Chemotherapy-Naive mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig (a novel therapy) combined with abiraterone against standard options (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone alone) in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not yet received chemotherapy. The primary goal is to measure overall survival. The trial is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: 177Lu-TLX591 Radioligand Therapy Plus Standard Care for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial evaluates 177Lu-TLX591 (a radioligand therapy) combined with standard treatment versus standard treatment alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who progressed after androgen receptor pathway inhibitor treatment. This is a targeted radiation approach similar to Lutetium-PSMA. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Apalutamide Plus Radiation for Recurrent Prostate Cancer After Surgery
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether adding enhanced therapy (apalutamide with abiraterone and prednisone) to standard prostate radiation and hormone therapy improves outcomes in patients with biochemical recurrence after prostate surgery. A second part tests adding targeted radiation for patients with metastases detected on PET scans. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Testosterone Plus ZEN-3694 Followed by Enzalutamide for Treatment-Resistant mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial investigates whether combining testosterone with ZEN-3694 (a BET inhibitor), followed by enzalutamide plus ZEN-3694, can shrink tumors in castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have failed other therapies. The approach tests whether testosterone priming may improve subsequent treatment effectiveness. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: First-in-Human Study of GSK5471713 for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 study evaluates a new investigational drug GSK5471713 as a single therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. It will assess safety, how the body processes the drug, early effectiveness, and establish appropriate dosing. The trial is recruiting patients.

items.title: GSK5458514 Alone or Combined With Other Agents for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial tests GSK5458514, a novel investigational drug, given alone or with other anti-cancer treatments in prostate cancer patients. The study includes dose escalation to find the right dose and expansion to assess effectiveness. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Abiraterone as First-Line Treatment for mCRPC in China
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial evaluates olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) combined with abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone as first-line therapy for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients in China who have not received chemotherapy or new hormone agents. The trial is no longer recruiting but remains active.

items.title: Treatment Intensification for Patients Not Achieving Deep PSA Response
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests whether adding docetaxel chemotherapy to apalutamide and ADT improves outcomes in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients who did not achieve a deep PSA response (PSA ≤0.2 or 90% reduction with PSA ≤4) after initial apalutamide treatment. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Abemaciclib With or Without Atezolizumab for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tested whether abemaciclib (a targeted chemotherapy) and atezolizumab (an immunotherapy), alone or combined, can shrink or prevent growth of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial evaluated safety of the combination and is now completed.

items.title: Safety and Effectiveness Study of ABBV-969 for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial assesses ABBV-969, an investigational drug, as a single treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study includes dose escalation and dose selection phases to determine the recommended Phase 2 dose. The trial is no longer recruiting new patients but remains active.

items.title: PSMA-Targeted Radioligand Therapy for Low-Volume Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tests whether adding 177Lu-PSMA-617 (a targeted radiation therapy) to hormone therapy, with or without abiraterone and prednisone, improves outcomes in patients with hormone-sensitive prostate cancer that has spread to a limited number of sites. The trial will begin recruiting soon.

items.title: Tarlatamab for DLL3-Positive Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial evaluates tarlatamab in patients with DLL3-positive prostate cancer that has metastasized and either relapsed or not responded to treatment. The study aims to determine if tarlatamab is an effective treatment for this specific biomarker-defined patient population. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Low Dose Naltrexone for Fatigue in Prostate Cancer Patients
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial tests whether low-dose naltrexone (3 mg daily) can reduce fatigue in men with prostate cancer receiving hormone therapy (ADT) with or without newer hormone medicines like apalutamide, enzalutamide, or abiraterone. The trial will begin recruiting soon.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan With or Without Combinations for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial assesses ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, given alone or with other treatments in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluates safety, identifies safe combination doses, and measures PSA levels and treatment effectiveness. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Darolutamide and Abemaciclib With ADT for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial established the safety and recommended dose of combining darolutamide and abemaciclib with androgen deprivation therapy for metastatic, non-metastatic, and advanced prostate cancer. The study involved about 93 participants and is now completed.

items.title: Mevrometostat With or Without Enzalutamide for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial studies mevrometostat (an epigenetic therapy) alone or combined with enzalutamide in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer who progressed after previous CRPC treatment. The study includes assessment and maintenance phases. Currently recruiting for Part 3.

items.title: Adaptive Dosing Schedule for Lutetium-177 PSMA in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares different dosing schedules for lutetium-177 PSMA radioligand therapy in hormone-resistant prostate cancer. It tests whether lengthening the interval between doses improves quality of life without reducing survival, compared to the standard every-6-week dosing schedule. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan vs Chemotherapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) to chemotherapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The primary goal is to determine if patients receiving I-DXd live longer overall and live longer without cancer progression compared to those receiving chemotherapy. The trial is recruiting.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Progression
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation, particularly through NFκB and IL6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways, reshapes the biology of advanced prostate cancer. These inflammatory pathways work with androgen receptor signaling to promote tumor survival, growth, spread, and resistance to treatment. Understanding these mechanisms may identify new therapeutic targets.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances PD-1 Blockade Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a nanoplasmid-based DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein highly expressed in aggressive prostate cancer). The vaccine primed immune responses and enhanced effectiveness of PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor therapy in laboratory models, showing potential for combination immunotherapy approaches.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 Shows Limited Benefit Over Radium-223 Alone
items.source: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
items.summary: This Phase 2 randomized trial found that combining olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) with radium-223 did not significantly improve radiographic progression-free survival compared to radium-223 alone in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases. Most patients had received prior hormone therapy and about half had received docetaxel chemotherapy.

items.title: Cell-Free DNA Testing for Treatment Selection in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This review examines the use of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) from blood tests for guiding treatment decisions in metastatic prostate cancer. ctDNA testing offers advantages over tissue biopsies, including less invasiveness and the ability to repeat testing over time. The review discusses current evidence, clinical interpretation principles, and future applications in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Resistance in mCRPC
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a new drug (compound 21d) that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT pathways to overcome c-MYC-driven resistance to AKT inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The dual inhibitor addresses a key resistance mechanism where elevated c-MYC expression limits effectiveness of AKT-targeted therapy alone.

items.title: Quality of Life Outcomes With Olaparib Plus Radium-223 in CRPC
items.summary: This analysis of patient-reported outcomes from the COMRADE trial assessed quality of life and pain in castration-resistant prostate cancer patients with bone metastases receiving olaparib plus radium-223 versus radium-223 alone. The study used validated questionnaires (FACT-P and BPI) to measure changes in symptoms and function over 24 weeks.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in mCRPC
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of 1,580 patients from 21 trials evaluated immune checkpoint inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without biomarker selection. Results showed 1-year survival of 63% and 2-year survival of 39%, with combination therapy showing better outcomes than single or dual checkpoint inhibitor therapy. The findings suggest checkpoint inhibitors show promise but limited benefit in unselected mCRPC patients.

items.title: Targeting Regulatory T Cells in Prostate Cancer Microenvironment
items.summary: This review examines how regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the prostate tumor microenvironment promote immune evasion and cancer progression. High stromal Treg density is associated with more than double the risk of biochemical recurrence. The review synthesizes spatial and single-cell data showing that Treg location and activation state, not just quantity, are critical for understanding their impact and developing targeted therapies.
